name: ratty
desc: GPU-rendered terminal emulator with inline 3D graphics
why: A GPU terminal rendering inline 3D graphics is a real hook, though terminal emulators are a crowded niche.

brief.what_it_is: Ratty is a terminal emulator, described on its homepage as a GPU-rendered terminal emulator with inline 3D graphics. The homepage's own page title reads "Ratty — A GPU-rendered terminal emulator with inline 3D graphics 🐀🧀". The homepage text I could read is nearly empty apart from that title and a few navigation links ("Read the blog post", "Download", "Source"), so I could not confirm what goes in or out beyond the tagline. The Homebrew entry lists a single executable, `ratty`.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated problem or motivation that I could read. The only framing available is the tagline, which says it is a terminal that renders inline 3D graphics.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew formula name and executable was visible. The homepage has a "Download" link, but I could not retrieve its target. No runtime, account, or first-run configuration was found.
brief.standout: The hook, from the tagline, is inline 3D graphics drawn inside a GPU-rendered terminal. The scout note calls terminal emulators a crowded niche, and that is fair, but the 3D-inline angle is the distinguishing claim. I could not verify how it is implemented or how well it works.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage loaded but had no release date, changelog, or commit information in the text I could read. A guessed GitHub URL (github.com/ratty-term/ratty) returned 404, and I did not find the real source repository link, so I have no commit or release evidence.
brief.caveats: The homepage was only partly readable: the body text appears to be JavaScript-rendered or otherwise missing, so the brief rests mostly on the title and the Homebrew description. No README was reached, so there are no commands, platform notes, licence, or build requirements. The brief therefore cannot confirm the 3D graphics claim beyond the marketing line.
